options: Cause an egg (in a follicle) to mature in the ovary
questions.explain: FSH, secreted by the pituitary gland, stimulates eggs to mature in the ovaries and triggers oestrogen release.

questions.q: Which is a barrier method of contraception that also helps prevent STIs?
questions.explain: Condoms are a barrier method that physically stop sperm reaching the egg and also reduce STI transmission.

questions.q: How does the contraceptive pill (containing oestrogen/progesterone) prevent pregnancy?
options: It inhibits FSH so no eggs mature
It kills sperm directly in the uterus
questions.explain: The hormones in the pill inhibit FSH production, so no eggs mature and ovulation does not occur.

questions.q: Compared with nervous responses, hormonal responses are generally:
questions.explain: Hormonal responses are slower to act but their effects last longer than fast, short-lived nervous responses.

questions.q: A plant shoot grows towards light. This response is called:
questions.explain: Growth towards light is positive phototropism, controlled by the hormone auxin.

questions.q: Which hormone causes the lining of the uterus to thicken during the menstrual cycle?
questions.explain: Oestrogen, produced by the ovaries, causes the uterus lining to build up ready for a possible pregnancy.

questions.q: When blood glucose falls too low, the pancreas releases glucagon, which causes the liver to:
questions.explain: Glucagon makes the liver convert stored glycogen back into glucose, raising blood glucose levels.

questions.q: During filtration in the kidney, which substance is NOT normally found in the filtrate of a healthy person?
questions.explain: Large proteins and blood cells are too big to be filtered, so they stay in the blood; glucose is filtered but reabsorbed.

options: A complete lack of a pancreas
The body's cells no longer responding properly to insulin
Too much insulin being produced from birth
questions.explain: In Type 2 diabetes cells stop responding to insulin; it is linked to obesity and often controlled by diet and exercise.

questions.q: Hormones are transported around the body in the:
questions.explain: Hormones are chemical messengers secreted by glands and carried in the blood to target organs.

options: The breakdown of glucose for energy
The maintenance of a constant internal environment
questions.explain: Homeostasis is the regulation of internal conditions, such as temperature and blood glucose, within set limits.

questions.q: How does meiosis differ from mitosis?
options: Meiosis halves the chromosome number and makes varied gametes; mitosis makes identical diploid cells
Mitosis makes gametes; meiosis makes body cells
questions.explain: Meiosis halves chromosome number to form varied gametes, whereas mitosis produces two genetically identical diploid cells.
